chunks: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from al-Husayn ibn Bashir who said:

I and al-Husayn ibn Qayama sought permission to meet al-Ridha (peace be upon him) in Surya, and he granted it to us. He said: 'Finish your needs.' Al-Husayn said to him: 'Will the earth be devoid of an Imam?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' He said: 'Will there be two [Imams] in it?' He said: 'No, except one who is silent and does not speak.' He said: 'Then I know that you are not an Imam!' He said: 'And how did you know that?' He said: 'You have no son, and [Imamate] is through the male line.' So he said to him: 'By Allah, the days and nights will not pass until a male is born to me from my loins who will assume a position like mine, he will enliven the truth and efface the falsehood.'

key_terms.صامت: Silent (referring to the Imam who is alive but not publicly active)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about the future birth of his son and the continuity of Imamate?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi's *Ikhtiyar* highlights the Shia doctrine of *Ismah* and the necessity of a living Imam (*al-Imam al-Hayy*) at all times, addressing the theological concern of the 'silent Imam' during periods of minor or major occultation. Al-Husayn ibn Qayama’s challenge regarding the lack of a known heir is resolved by Imam al-Rida’s prophecy of a son who will 'revive the truth and abolish falsehood,' a description often linked to Imam al-Mahdi (aj). This dialogue underscores the continuity of divine authority (*Hujjah*) from the Prophet through the Imams, ensuring the preservation of Islam until the Day of Judgment.
